# Saga: Local-GPU fine-tuning + agentic, tool-using `:ask`

## Vision

Reach the workflow where a user, inside the sw-MLPL REPL, can:

1. Fine-tune a small but REAL local model on the GPU (MLX on Apple
   Silicon, CUDA on Linux) and SEE measurable learning happen.
2. Ask Ollama for help with that fine-tuning -- an agentic,
   tool-using `:ask` that REQUESTS the training context it needs
   (loss curve, hyperparameters, model shape) and answers from what
   it retrieved (Recursive-Language-Model-style tooling).

This merges the previously-planned agentic-`:ask` work
(`docs/agentic-ask-plan.md`) with a new "Local GPU" demo group.

## Foundation already in place

- **Connect mode (SSE).** `?connect=<url>` routes REPL eval to
  `mlpl-serve`, executed server-side. `connect.rs` +
  `eval_wasm::connect_eval`.
- **Contextual `:ask` + real system role (shipped).** `llm_call`
  takes an optional 4th `system` arg -> Ollama's `system` field;
  web `:ask` sends the question as the user prompt and the sw-MLPL
  grounding + REPL history + selected-sculpture context as the
  system message. Plus `:history`, the in-dialog Ask button,
  `?ollama=` / `?model=`.
- **LoRA fine-tuning of MLPL-native models.** `lora(m, rank,
  alpha, seed)` wraps every `Linear` with adapters; `adam(loss,
  lora_m, ...)` updates ONLY the adapters. MLX device support
  (`device("mlx")`, `mlpl-mlx-rt`, `mlpl-mlx-serve`). Working demos:
  `demos/lora_finetune.mlpl`, `demos/lora_finetune_mlx.mlpl`.

## Policy decisions (load-bearing -- bake into every step)

### Model acquisition: demo-initiated, allow-listed, never silent

The headline demo DOWNLOADS the pretrained model as its first step
(measure -> fine-tune -> re-measure -> show improvement). That is
allowed because the user PERMITS it by choosing to run the demo --
it is not a silent or background fetch. The guardrails that keep it
inside the "no large downloads without permission" rule:

- **Named + allow-listed, never an arbitrary URL.** A narrow builtin
  (e.g. `fetch_pretrained("smollm2-135m")`) maps a SHORT allow-listed
  NAME to a pinned source + cache path. There is NO `download(url)`.
- **Size disclosed up front.** The demo states the download size
  (e.g. "~270MB SmolLM2-135M, one time, cached") before fetching, and
  skips re-download if already cached.
- **Server-side in connect mode.** The browser cannot write the
  user's disk; in connect mode `mlpl-serve` performs the allow-listed
  fetch + cache. The download is therefore connect-only (the public
  GitHub Pages demo marks it visible-but-not-runnable).
- **CLI mirrors it.** The CLI demo runs the same allow-listed fetch
  locally (or reads an already-pulled model by path), then the same
  measure / fine-tune / re-measure arc.

Ollama-served inference still uses `ollama pull smollm2:135m`; the
FINE-TUNING path needs raw weights (safetensors/bf16), which is what
`fetch_pretrained` caches.

### External IO: narrow capabilities, no general shell

No general `sh()` / `run()` / `curl` escape. The web playground
runs UNTRUSTED pasted input and the server runs `--auth disabled`
on loopback -- arbitrary shell there is remote code execution.
Pattern: narrow, purpose-built, allow-listed builtins (like the
existing `llm_call`). Web/WASM builds get NO shell and NO arbitrary
network. Any future shell-like capability is native-CLI-only, off
by default behind an explicit `--allow-shell` flag, never compiled
into WASM.

## "Measurable learning" -- the success metric

Every training/fine-tuning demo must assert a measurable delta on
HELD-OUT data, not just a falling train loss:

- Language models: validation cross-entropy / perplexity /
  bits-per-char dropping over steps, plus before/after text samples.

1	# Saga: Local-GPU fine-tuning + agentic, tool-using `:ask`
2	
3	## Vision
4	
5	Reach the workflow where a user, inside the sw-MLPL REPL, can:
6	
7	1. Fine-tune a small but REAL local model on the GPU (MLX on Apple
8	   Silicon, CUDA on Linux) and SEE measurable learning happen.
9	2. Ask Ollama for help with that fine-tuning -- an agentic,
10	   tool-using `:ask` that REQUESTS the training context it needs
11	   (loss curve, hyperparameters, model shape) and answers from what
12	   it retrieved (Recursive-Language-Model-style tooling).
13	
14	This merges the previously-planned agentic-`:ask` work
15	(`docs/agentic-ask-plan.md`) with a new "Local GPU" demo group.
16	
17	## Foundation already in place
18	
19	- **Connect mode (SSE).** `?connect=<url>` routes REPL eval to
20	  `mlpl-serve`, executed server-side. `connect.rs` +
21	  `eval_wasm::connect_eval`.
22	- **Contextual `:ask` + real system role (shipped).** `llm_call`
23	  takes an optional 4th `system` arg -> Ollama's `system` field;
24	  web `:ask` sends the question as the user prompt and the sw-MLPL
25	  grounding + REPL history + selected-sculpture context as the
26	  system message. Plus `:history`, the in-dialog Ask button,
27	  `?ollama=` / `?model=`.
28	- **LoRA fine-tuning of MLPL-native models.** `lora(m, rank,
29	  alpha, seed)` wraps every `Linear` with adapters; `adam(loss,
30	  lora_m, ...)` updates ONLY the adapters. MLX device support
31	  (`device("mlx")`, `mlpl-mlx-rt`, `mlpl-mlx-serve`). Working demos:
32	  `demos/lora_finetune.mlpl`, `demos/lora_finetune_mlx.mlpl`.
33	
34	## Policy decisions (load-bearing -- bake into every step)
35	
36	### Model acquisition: demo-initiated, allow-listed, never silent
37	
38	The headline demo DOWNLOADS the pretrained model as its first step
39	(measure -> fine-tune -> re-measure -> show improvement). That is
40	allowed because the user PERMITS it by choosing to run the demo --
41	it is not a silent or background fetch. The guardrails that keep it
42	inside the "no large downloads without permission" rule:
43	
44	- **Named + allow-listed, never an arbitrary URL.** A narrow builtin
45	  (e.g. `fetch_pretrained("smollm2-135m")`) maps a SHORT allow-listed
46	  NAME to a pinned source + cache path. There is NO `download(url)`.
47	- **Size disclosed up front.** The demo states the download size
48	  (e.g. "~270MB SmolLM2-135M, one time, cached") before fetching, and
49	  skips re-download if already cached.
50	- **Server-side in connect mode.** The browser cannot write the
51	  user's disk; in connect mode `mlpl-serve` performs the allow-listed
52	  fetch + cache. The download is therefore connect-only (the public
53	  GitHub Pages demo marks it visible-but-not-runnable).
54	- **CLI mirrors it.** The CLI demo runs the same allow-listed fetch
55	  locally (or reads an already-pulled model by path), then the same
56	  measure / fine-tune / re-measure arc.
57	
58	Ollama-served inference still uses `ollama pull smollm2:135m`; the
59	FINE-TUNING path needs raw weights (safetensors/bf16), which is what
60	`fetch_pretrained` caches.
61	
62	### External IO: narrow capabilities, no general shell
63	
64	No general `sh()` / `run()` / `curl` escape. The web playground
65	runs UNTRUSTED pasted input and the server runs `--auth disabled`
66	on loopback -- arbitrary shell there is remote code execution.
67	Pattern: narrow, purpose-built, allow-listed builtins (like the
68	existing `llm_call`). Web/WASM builds get NO shell and NO arbitrary
69	network. Any future shell-like capability is native-CLI-only, off
70	by default behind an explicit `--allow-shell` flag, never compiled
71	into WASM.
72	
73	## Demo capability tiers (device gating)
74	
75	Demos declare a capability tier; the UI gates them by it. MLX
76	(Apple GPU) and CUDA (NVIDIA/Linux GPU) are SEPARATE groups; both
77	are connect-only + device-specific and NOT runnable on the public
78	GitHub Pages live demo. CPU-based training IS runnable on the live
79	demo (the in-browser WASM interpreter runs it, slowly).
80	
81	| Tier | Runs on live demo? | Needs | Examples |
82	|------|--------------------|-------|----------|
83	| `cpu` | YES (in-browser WASM) | nothing | tiny LoRA fine-tune (the 6.12 -> 1.34 run), core playground |
84	| `connect` | NO (needs a server) | `mlpl-serve` | contextual `:ask` (Ollama), `:models ollama` |
85	| `mlx` | NO | `mlpl-serve` + Mac MLX peer | MLX-accelerated demos (Apple Silicon) |
86	| `cuda` | NO (future) | `mlpl-serve` + Linux CUDA peer | future CUDA-accelerated demos |
87	
88	Registry flag shape (Phase 1): each demo carries
89	`{ requires_connect: bool, device: cpu|mlx|cuda }`. The public
90	build renders `connect`/`mlx`/`cuda` demos visible-but-not-runnable
91	with a "needs a connected mlpl-serve (+ <device> peer)" affordance;
92	`cpu` demos run everywhere.
93	
94	## RESOLVED (step 010, 2026-05-31): MLX LoRA training is now full-GPU
95	
96	The limitation described below is FIXED for the LoRA fine-tune path.
97	Under `device("mlx")`, `eval_adam` now detects a head-only LoRA model
98	(the demo architecture) and runs the whole fine-tune step on the GPU:
99	the loss is built as an `mlx_rs`-traceable graph over the adapters
100	(`mlpl-mlx-model::demo_forward`), differentiated by `value_and_grad`,
101	and the adapters are updated by an MLX-resident Adam (`adam_update`),
102	with moments persisted in `env.optim_state` across steps. Any other
103	model/device falls back to the CPU tape path. Parity-tested vs CPU in
104	`lora_mlx_demo_tests.rs` (loss curve within fp32 tol; frozen base
105	bit-identical). The `MLX LoRA fine-tune` demo is relabeled true-GPU.
106	General (non-LoRA) `device("mlx")` training still uses the CPU tape;
107	the section below documents that original state.
108	
109	## CRITICAL reality: MLX training was forward-only on the GPU (pre-step-010)
110	
111	Server-side MLX does NOT yet run a full training loop on the GPU.
112	With `device("mlx")`, only the FORWARD pass (matmul, attention,
113	softmax, cross-entropy) dispatches to MLX via `mlpl-mlx-rt`; the
114	BACKWARD pass (autograd in `mlpl-autograd`) and the adam optimizer
115	updates (`mlpl-eval/src/grad_optim.rs`, plain `Vec<f64>` math) run
116	on CPU. `mlpl-mlx-rt` exports forward ops only -- no MLX
117	backward/gradient/optimizer. So `device("mlx") { train { adam } }`
118	is a HYBRID (forward on GPU, backward+update on CPU), confirmed by
119	`grad_mlx_tests.rs` / `tiny_lm_mlx_demo_tests.rs` (parity, not GPU
120	execution of the backward/update).
121	
122	Consequence for the plan:
123	
124	- A NEW phase is required to make the full fine-tune loop run on the
125	  GPU: implement MLX backward + an MLX-resident adam (extend
126	  `mlpl-mlx-rt` + the autograd/optimizer path so gradients and
127	  moment buffers stay on-device, no per-step CPU round-trip).
128	- Until that lands, the MLX demo must be HONESTLY labeled as
129	  "forward pass on GPU; gradient + optimizer on CPU" -- not
130	  "training runs on the GPU".
131	
132	### Step 004 scoping (2026-05-31): code map + the architecture fork
133	
134	A read-through of the relevant crates (no build) pins the work:
135	
136	- **`mlpl-mlx-rt`** (`components/native-rt/crates/`): 7 modules of
137	  FORWARD ops only (matmul, add/sub/mul/div/neg, exp/log/relu/sigmoid/
138	  tanh, softmax/log_softmax/cross_entropy/mean/reduce_mul/argmax,
139	  transpose/reshape). MLX arrays are `mlx_rs::Array`; ops are free
140	  functions; everything triple-gated
141	  `cfg(all(target_os="macos", target_arch="aarch64", feature="mlx"))`.
142	  No backward/gradient/optimizer op exists.
143	- **Forward dispatch** lives in `mlpl-eval/src/device.rs`
144	  (`try_mlx_dispatch`, `dispatched_call`): only fires when
145	  `env.device()=="mlx"`. Device is a `String` on `Environment`'s
146	  device stack -- it does NOT travel on the tensor/tape node level.
147	- **`mlpl-autograd`**: the tape is CPU f64; `backward.rs` has 19
148	  functions and carries NO device info. The MLX hook
149	  (`materialize_tape_on_mlx`) only round-trips forward VALUES to fp32
150	  so CPU backward matches MLX within tolerance -- backward itself is
151	  always CPU.
152	- **adam** (`mlpl-eval/src/grad_optim.rs`): moment buffers are
153	  `Vec<f64>` in `Environment::optim_state`; every step calls
154	  `eval_grad` (CPU tape build + backward) and does the update in f64.
155	  A full per-step CPU round-trip.
156	
157	**Architecture fork (decide in step 005 BEFORE implementing):**
158	
159	- **A) MLX built-in autodiff (recommended).** Express the MLX
160	  fine-tune step's forward as an `mlx_rs`-traceable function and use
161	  `value_and_grad`/`grad` for on-device gradients; keep moment buffers
162	  as `mlx_rs::Array`. Bypasses the 19 hand-written backward formulas
163	  for the MLX path -- far less code, no parity drift -- at the cost of
164	  restructuring the MLX loop to build an MLX graph rather than the CPU
165	  tape.
166	- **B) Hand-port backward to MLX.** Add MLX backward ops to
167	  `mlpl-mlx-rt` and make `mlpl-autograd` dispatch backward to MLX when
168	  `device=="mlx"`, plus an on-device adam. Keeps the tape architecture
169	  but is ~19 formulas to port and parity-maintain.
170	
171	**sw-checklist note:** `backward.rs` (19 fns) and `mlpl-mlx-rt`
172	(`reductions.rs` 7 fns; 7 modules) are already over budget. Splitting
173	`backward.rs` into sibling files would push the crate past the
174	7-module FAIL line -- trading one FAIL for another. The correct fix is
175	a sibling crate (e.g. `mlpl-autograd-backward`) inside the autograd
176	component with dependency inversion (`Tensor::backward()` must not
177	re-enter), which is its own step, not incidental paydown.
178	
179	**Decomposition:** step 004 = scope + decompose + disk recovery (the
180	shared `target/` had grown to 40 GB with 24 GiB free; cleared to 63
181	GiB free). Step **005 (`mlx-fullgpu-architecture-spike`)** resolves
182	the fork with a small spike build and defines the implementation
183	follow-ons (approach A: traceable-forward then value_and_grad+adam;
184	approach B: mlx-rt backward -> autograd dispatch -> on-device adam),
185	each parity-tested vs CPU within fp32 tolerance, ending with the
186	demo relabeled hybrid -> true-GPU.
187	
188	### Step 005 result (2026-05-31): approach A DECIDED + spike proven
189	
190	**Decision: approach A** (MLX built-in autodiff). The vendored
191	`mlx-rs` (0.25.3) exposes `transforms::value_and_grad` /
192	`value_and_grad_with_argnums` (closure `|&[Array]| -> Result<Vec<Array>>`
193	-> `(values, grads)`) AND an `optimizers` module (Adam/AdamW/Adamax).
194	So the MLX fine-tune step can be differentiated on-device with zero
195	hand-written backward formulas -- approach B (porting ~19 formulas) is
196	abandoned.
197	
198	**Spike (proven, parity-tested):** new sibling crate
199	`components/native-rt/crates/mlpl-mlx-train` ("refactor up and out":
200	training is a distinct concern from the forward-only `mlpl-mlx-rt`,
201	so its own crate; native-rt now has 3 crates, within the <=4 budget;
202	sw-checklist 6 passed / 0 failed / 0 warnings). It provides:
203	
204	- `loss_and_grads(params, loss_fn)` -- wraps `value_and_grad_with_argnums`
205	  over all params; returns the scalar loss + one gradient `Array` each.
206	- `MlxAdam` -- Adam whose m/v moment buffers ARE `mlx_rs::Array`; the
207	  update is pure MLX elementwise ops, so gradients and optimizer state
208	  never leave the device.
209	
210	Two gated tests pass on Apple Silicon (`cargo test -p mlpl-mlx-train
211	--features mlx`): `value_and_grad` matches the analytic least-squares
212	gradient at w=0 (parity), and `MlxAdam` drives a tiny regression to
213	the closed-form solution. Forward + backward + optimizer all on MLX.
214	`mlx-sys` builds in ~80s with `accelerate` (no Metal/Xcode needed).
215	
216	**Next (step 006, `mlx-finetune-loop-value-and-grad`):** wire this
217	into the real MLX LoRA fine-tune loop. When `device("mlx")`, the
218	fine-tune step builds its loss as a traceable closure over the LoRA
219	adapter params and uses `loss_and_grads` + `MlxAdam` instead of the
220	CPU tape (`mlpl-autograd`) + CPU adam (`grad_optim.rs`). Parity-test
221	the LoRA loss curve vs the CPU path within fp32 tolerance, then
222	relabel the `MLX LoRA fine-tune` demo hybrid -> true-GPU. The CPU
223	`backward.rs` 19-fn FAIL is now orthogonal debt (approach A bypasses
224	it for the MLX path); retire it separately via the sibling-crate split.
225	
226	### Step 006 slice (2026-05-31): on-device LoRA training kernel proven
227	
228	`mlpl-mlx-train` now has the full on-device training kernel and proves
229	the LoRA mechanism end-to-end (it was the linreg spike before):
230	
231	- `lora_linear(x, w, a, b, scale)` -- the traceable LoRA forward
232	  `x @ (w + scale*(a@b))` in MLX ops, differentiable w.r.t. the
233	  adapters.
234	- `train_steps(params, adam, n, loss_fn)` -- runs the on-device loop
235	  (forward + `value_and_grad` backward + `MlxAdam` update), returning
236	  the loss curve. Nothing round-trips to the CPU.
237	
238	Two gated tests pass on Apple Silicon: `value_and_grad` matches a
239	finite-difference gradient over BOTH adapters (parity), and `MlxAdam`
240	drives a frozen-base + rank-1-adapter problem to a collapsed loss.
241	Crate stays clean (4 modules, sw-checklist 6 passed / 0 failed / 0
242	warnings). MLX's `value_and_grad` mutates global trace state and is
243	not thread-safe, so the gradient tests serialize on a crate-local
244	`MLX_TEST_LOCK` (the parallel eager parity tests in `mlpl-mlx-rt` are
245	unaffected) -- do not run grad tests in parallel.
246	
247	**Remaining for the demo (step 007, `mlx-finetune-model-forward`):**
248	express the FULL demo model forward -- embed (one-hot matmul), causal
249	attention, rms_norm, linear, cross_entropy -- as `mlx_rs::Array` ops
250	(the interpreter forward is eager/CPU-materialized and cannot be
251	traced as-is), assemble it into the `train_steps` loss closure over
252	the LoRA adapters, wire it into `eval_adam`'s MLX path (read base
253	params + adapters from the Environment, write adapters back each
254	step), parity-test the loss curve vs the CPU path
255	(`lora_mlx_demo_tests.rs`) within fp32 tol, then relabel the demo
256	hybrid -> true-GPU. This forward reimplementation is the bulk; split
257	into its own crate (e.g. `mlpl-mlx-forward`) if it grows the module
258	budget.
259	
260	### Step 007 slice (2026-05-31): forward primitives in MLX ops
261	
262	New crate `components/native-rt/crates/mlpl-mlx-forward` (native-rt now
263	4 crates, at the <=4 budget; sw-checklist 6 passed / 0 failed / 0
264	warnings) implements the non-attention forward primitives as
265	`mlx_rs::Array` ops, each parity-tested vs a hand-computed reference:
266	
267	- `embed(onehot, table)` -- embedding as a one-hot matmul (traceable +
268	  differentiable w.r.t. the table, unlike an index gather).
269	- `rms_norm(x, gamma, eps)` -- `x / sqrt(mean(x^2)+eps) * gamma`.
270	- `cross_entropy(logits, targets_onehot)` -- stable `logsumexp_axis`
271	  minus the picked logit, mean over rows.
272	
273	These are forward-VALUE tests (no `value_and_grad`), so they run in
274	parallel. Remaining for the demo: `causal_attention` (step 008), then
275	assemble the full forward into the `train_steps` loss closure, wire
276	into `eval_adam`'s MLX path, parity-test vs the CPU demo, and relabel
277	the demo true-GPU (step 009).
278	
279	### Step 008 slice (2026-05-31): causal attention
280	
281	`mlpl-mlx-forward` gains `attention.rs` (crate stays 4 modules / 0
282	warnings): `causal_attention(x, wq, wk, wv, wo, mask)` =
283	`softmax((Q Kᵀ)/sqrt(d_k) + mask) V` then the output projection, plus a
284	`causal_mask(t)` builder (0 on/below the diagonal, large-negative
285	above). Single-head (h=1, matching the demo's `causal_attention(d, 1,
286	_)`); multi-head per-head slabs are a later extension. Parity-tested
287	vs a hand-computed identity-weight case (T=2): row 0 attends only to
288	key 0, row 1 mixes by `softmax([0, 1/sqrt2])`.
289	
290	All forward primitives for the demo model now exist in MLX ops
291	(embed, rms_norm, causal_attention, linear via `lora_linear`,
292	cross_entropy). Step 009 assembles them into the `train_steps` loss
293	closure, wires `eval_adam`'s MLX-LoRA path, parity-tests the loss
294	curve vs the CPU demo, and relabels the demo true-GPU.
295	
296	### Step 009 slice (2026-05-31): the full demo model trains on MLX
297	
298	New component `components/mlx-model/crates/mlpl-mlx-model` (its own
299	component so native-rt stays at 4 crates; sw-checklist 7 passed / 0
300	failed / 0 warnings) assembles the demo architecture into one traceable
301	graph:
302	
303	- `DemoWeights` -- the frozen base weights (embed table, attention
304	  Wq/Wk/Wv/Wo, head W + bias, an all-ones gamma, causal mask).
305	- `demo_forward(weights, adapters, x_onehot, y_onehot)` -- runs
306	  `embed -> rms_norm -> causal_attention -> (residual) -> rms_norm ->
307	  lora head -> cross_entropy`. Base weights are captured constants; the
308	  traced params are the head's single `[A, B]` adapter pair.
309	
310	A gated test trains the adapters with `MlxAdam` via `train_steps` and
311	asserts the cross-entropy drops -- gradients flow through the WHOLE
312	assembled model and the optimizer reduces the loss, all on the GPU.
313	This is the last technical unknown; what remains is interpreter glue.
314	
315	### Step 010 progress (2026-05-31): exact CPU-match findings
316	
317	Wiring requires `demo_forward` to match the CPU `apply_model` EXACTLY
318	(else the parity test diverges). Reading the CPU primitives corrected
319	several wrong assumptions (the forward is now fixed accordingly):
320	
321	- **RMSNorm is gamma-free**, `eps = 1e-8` (`model_apply_compose.rs`):
322	  `y = x / sqrt(mean(x^2) + eps)`. The `RmsNorm` layer has NO params
323	  (`params()` returns empty), so the MLX path passes an all-ones gamma.
324	- **Only the head is LoRA-adapted.** `lora()` rewrites `Linear` ->
325	  `LinearLora`, but the attention projections live in the separate
326	  `Attention { wq, wk, wv, wo }` variant, NOT `Linear` -- so they stay
327	  FROZEN. The demo therefore has ONE adapter pair (`__lora_A_0`,
328	  `__lora_B_0`) on the head, not one per projection.
329	- **The head LoRA carries a bias** (`model_apply_lora.rs`):
330	  `x @ w + (alpha/rank) * (x @ a @ b) + b`.
331	- **Attention** (h=1, `model_apply_attention.rs`): `scale = 1/sqrt(d_k)`,
332	  `d_k = d_model/heads`; matches `causal_attention` for the single-head
333	  demo.
334	
335	So `mlpl-mlx-model` now also exposes the converters it needs:
336	`mlpl-mlx-rt::{dense_to_mlx, mlx_to_dense_data, Array}` are now public.
337	
338	**Remaining (the finish):** add `mlpl-mlx-train` + `mlpl-mlx-model` to
339	`mlpl-eval`'s `mlx` feature; a new `grad_optim_mlx.rs` that, when
340	`device("mlx")` and the only non-frozen params are the head adapters
341	AND the model matches the demo shape (else fall back to CPU): walks the
342	student `ModelSpec` for the frozen weights + adapter names, extracts X/Y
343	from the `cross_entropy(apply(model, X), Y)` loss expr, builds one-hots,
344	runs one `loss_and_grads` + a stateless MLX adam update per step
345	(persisting m/v in `env.optim_state` like the CPU path), writes the
346	adapters back. Branch at the top of `eval_adam`. Then assert the
347	`device("mlx")` loss curve matches the CPU path in `lora_mlx_demo_tests.rs`
348	within fp32 tol, and relabel the `MLX LoRA fine-tune` demo hybrid ->
349	true-GPU. (Apple-only glue; see the CUDA-pivot note below.)
350	
351	## "Measurable learning" -- the success metric
352	
353	Every training/fine-tuning demo must assert a measurable delta on
354	HELD-OUT data, not just a falling train loss:
355	
356	- Language models: validation cross-entropy / perplexity /
357	  bits-per-char dropping over steps, plus before/after text samples.
358	- Classification / synthetic tasks: validation accuracy rising.
359	- The demo prints the metric at step 0 and at the end and a smoke
360	  test asserts the improvement, so "learning happened" is checkable.
361	
362	## The ~100MB model: SmolLM2-135M (finale), de-risked first
363	
364	Target: **SmolLM2-135M** -- a real, instruction-tuned 135M-param
365	model (~135MB q4 via Ollama; ~270MB bf16 for LoRA training). It is
366	Ollama-compatible, so the same model can be served for inference AND
367	be the subject of "ask Ollama for fine-tuning help."
368	
369	Because loading + fine-tuning a real pretrained transformer is the
370	biggest unknown, de-risk in order:
371	
372	1. Showcase measurable learning on the EXISTING MLPL-native MLX LoRA
373	   path first (it already runs).
374	2. Then build the SmolLM2 loader + LLaMA-style architecture +
375	   tokenizer.
376	
377	### Known gaps for the SmolLM2 finale
378	
379	- Weight loader: no `safetensors` / `GGUF` reader yet.
380	- Architecture ops: RoPE, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, grouped-query attention
381	  are not present (SmolLM2 is a LLaMA-style decoder).
382	- Tokenizer: SmolLM2's BPE vocab/merges.
383	
384	## Phased plan
385	
386	- **Phase 0 -- Ollama settings exposure.** Server-owned default
387	  host + model (config / flags / `OLLAMA_HOST`); `GET <host>/api/tags`
388	  -> a `:models ollama` listing + UI picker. (Per-`:ask --model`
389	  override DEFERRED at user request.)
390	- **Phase 1 -- Demo capability tiers + gating.** Tag every demo
391	  with `{ requires_connect, device: cpu|mlx|cuda }`. Separate demo
392	  sections for `connect`, `mlx`, and (future) `cuda`; `cpu` demos
393	  (incl. the tiny LoRA fine-tune) run on the public live demo,
394	  GPU/connect demos render visible-but-not-runnable there. Seed:
395	  the CPU LoRA fine-tune (live, measurable 6.12->1.34) and the
396	  contextual `:ask` (connect). The MLX section's training entry is
397	  HONESTLY labeled "forward on GPU, backward+adam on CPU" until the
398	  phase below lands.
399	- **Phase 1b -- Full MLX GPU training loop.** Make the fine-tune
400	  loop actually run on the GPU: MLX backward + MLX-resident adam
401	  (extend `mlpl-mlx-rt` and the autograd/optimizer path so
402	  gradients + moment buffers stay on-device, no per-step CPU
403	  round-trip). Only after this is the MLX demo a true GPU
404	  fine-tune. CUDA is the same shape on a Linux peer (later).
405	- **Phase 1c -- Viz passthrough ("3D everywhere").** The UI -- the
406	  3D view especially -- should show results regardless of WHERE the
407	  work ran (local WASM, the MLX peer, a future CUDA peer). Today the
408	  connect-mode eval response is just `{value, kind}` (a display
409	  string), so server-evaluated lines emit NO 3D. Make the eval
410	  response carry viz data so the client emits the 3D event for ANY
411	  result: (1) `shape` + flat `values` (+ `string_list`) first --
412	  covers basic tensor/grid/bar sculptures, no new serialization;
413	  (2) `viz_node` later (attention heatmaps, Sankey) -- requires
414	  making `VizNode` (mlpl-web-viz-ir) `Serialize`/`Deserialize` and
415	  extracting it server-side (today that lives in `mlpl-wasm`'s
416	  `eval_with_values`, not a shared crate). This is the GATE that
417	  lets `device("mlx")`/`device("cuda")` blocks route to the server
418	  (GPU) WITHOUT losing 3D -- the real form of the web MLX demo. The
419	  `mlpl-serve` `mlx` feature (shipped) is the server-side half.
420	- **Phase 2 -- Agentic tool-using `:ask`.** Server-side
421	  `/api/chat` loop with `tools`: the model requests context
422	  (`get_recent_history`, `get_workspace_vars`, `describe_variable`,
423	  `get_selected_sculpture`, `get_builtin_help`, `get_demo_source`)
424	  and answers from what it retrieved. Surface the tool-call trace.
425	- **Phase 3 -- RLM "ask for help" demo.** A demo that fine-tunes on
426	  the GPU, then issues an agentic `:ask` ("why did the loss
427	  plateau?"). The model calls the context tools (loss history,
428	  hyperparameters) and advises -- the visible RLM loop.
429	- **Phase 4 -- SmolLM2-135M loader + architecture.** safetensors/
430	  GGUF reader, LLaMA-style ops (RoPE/RMSNorm/SwiGLU/GQA), SmolLM2
431	  BPE tokenizer; load weights by path and run a forward pass that
432	  matches a reference.
433	- **Phase 5 -- The headline demo: download -> measure -> fine-tune
434	  -> re-measure -> show improvement.** One demo (web in connect mode
435	  + a CLI twin) that: (1) `fetch_pretrained("smollm2-135m")` with
436	  size disclosure + cache; (2) measures baseline held-out perplexity
437	  + shows a baseline generation; (3) LoRA fine-tunes on a small
438	  target corpus on the GPU; (4) re-measures perplexity + shows a
439	  post-fine-tune generation; (5) asserts + displays the improvement.
440	  Then an agentic `:ask` advises on the fine-tune from the real
441	  metrics, and the result can be served via Ollama.
442	
443	## 3D dimension orientation (cross-cutting, normative)
444	
445	All 3D sculptures must follow `docs/3d-orientation.md`: longest
446	dimension recedes toward the mountains (-Z), 2nd-longest rises to
447	the sky (+Y), 3rd spreads left/right (X); stacked maps (attention
448	heads, conv channels) lay out as a row of maps receding along -Z.
449	Phase 1c part 1 fixed the per-head attention overlay

456	- `docs/SmolLM2-demo-plan.md` -- the pre-existing SmolLM2 135M

# Saga: Local-GPU fine-tuning + agentic, tool-using `:ask`

## Vision

Reach the workflow where a user, inside the sw-MLPL REPL, can:

1. Fine-tune a small but REAL local model on the GPU (MLX on Apple
   Silicon, CUDA on Linux) and SEE measurable learning happen.
2. Ask Ollama for help with that fine-tuning -- an agentic,
   tool-using `:ask` that REQUESTS the training context it needs
   (loss curve, hyperparameters, model shape) and answers from what
   it retrieved (Recursive-Language-Model-style tooling).

This merges the previously-planned agentic-`:ask` work
(`docs/agentic-ask-plan.md`) with a new "Local GPU" demo group.

## Foundation already in place

- **Connect mode (SSE).** `?connect=<url>` routes REPL eval to
  `mlpl-serve`, executed server-side. `connect.rs` +
  `eval_wasm::connect_eval`.
- **Contextual `:ask` + real system role (shipped).** `llm_call`
  takes an optional 4th `system` arg -> Ollama's `system` field;
  web `:ask` sends the question as the user prompt and the sw-MLPL
  grounding + REPL history + selected-sculpture context as the
  system message. Plus `:history`, the in-dialog Ask button,
  `?ollama=` / `?model=`.
- **LoRA fine-tuning of MLPL-native models.** `lora(m, rank,
  alpha, seed)` wraps every `Linear` with adapters; `adam(loss,
  lora_m, ...)` updates ONLY the adapters. MLX device support
  (`device("mlx")`, `mlpl-mlx-rt`, `mlpl-mlx-serve`). Working demos:
  `demos/lora_finetune.mlpl`, `demos/lora_finetune_mlx.mlpl`.

## Policy decisions (load-bearing -- bake into every step)

### Model acquisition: demo-initiated, allow-listed, never silent

The headline demo DOWNLOADS the pretrained model as its first step
(measure -> fine-tune -> re-measure -> show improvement). That is
allowed because the user PERMITS it by choosing to run the demo --
it is not a silent or background fetch. The guardrails that keep it
inside the "no large downloads without permission" rule:

- **Named + allow-listed, never an arbitrary URL.** A narrow builtin
  (e.g. `fetch_pretrained("smollm2-135m")`) maps a SHORT allow-listed
  NAME to a pinned source + cache path. There is NO `download(url)`.
- **Size disclosed up front.** The demo states the download size
  (e.g. "~270MB SmolLM2-135M, one time, cached") before fetching, and
  skips re-download if already cached.
- **Server-side in connect mode.** The browser cannot write the
  user's disk; in connect mode `mlpl-serve` performs the allow-listed
  fetch + cache. The download is therefore connect-only (the public
  GitHub Pages demo marks it visible-but-not-runnable).
- **CLI mirrors it.** The CLI demo runs the same allow-listed fetch
  locally (or reads an already-pulled model by path), then the same
  measure / fine-tune / re-measure arc.

Ollama-served inference still uses `ollama pull smollm2:135m`; the
FINE-TUNING path needs raw weights (safetensors/bf16), which is what
`fetch_pretrained` caches.

### External IO: narrow capabilities, no general shell

No general `sh()` / `run()` / `curl` escape. The web playground
runs UNTRUSTED pasted input and the server runs `--auth disabled`
on loopback -- arbitrary shell there is remote code execution.
Pattern: narrow, purpose-built, allow-listed builtins (like the
existing `llm_call`). Web/WASM builds get NO shell and NO arbitrary
network. Any future shell-like capability is native-CLI-only, off
by default behind an explicit `--allow-shell` flag, never compiled

backward/gradient/optimizer. So `device("mlx") { train { adam } }`

HELD-OUT data, not just a falling train loss:

- Language models: validation cross-entropy / perplexity /
  bits-per-char dropping over steps, plus before/after text samples.
- Classification / synthetic tasks: validation accuracy rising.
- The demo prints the metric at step 0 and at the end and a smoke
  test asserts the improvement, so "learning happened" is checkable.

be the subject of "ask Ollama for fine-tuning help."

40	`3 5 1`; regression tests in `mlpl-eval/tests/fn_scope.rs`.

43	
44	A recursive call overwrites the caller's locals, so a function that
45	binds a local, recurses, then reads that local gets the deepest frame's
46	value.
47	
48	Repro:
49	
50	```
51	def u:f(n) { if gt(n, 0) { keep = n; tmp = u:f(n - 1); keep } else { 0 } }
52	[u:f(3), u:f(5), u:f(1)]
53	```

1. **fn-scope** -- DONE (c40f9a68). `call_user_fn` snapshots/restores
   the variable namespaces per call; local writes do not leak to caller
   / siblings; outer reads still work. Regression tests in
   `fn_scope.rs` (recursion-with-locals, factorial, no-leak). (Fixed C1.)
2. **multiline-array** -- DONE (aeb480e2). `parse_array_lit` skips
   newlines inside `[ ]`; a multi-line matrix parses. Tests in
   `multiline_array_tests.rs`. (Fixed C2. Call-arg `( )` newlines remain
   a future nicety, not needed for matrix literals.)
3. **bare-if-diagnostic** -- DONE (d36b91fa). `else` is optional;
   statement-position `if` parses and evaluates (`0` when not taken).
   (Fixed C3.)

### Saga: interpreter-and-search-performance

Make recursive / array-heavy MLPL fast enough for real algorithms.

1. **alpha-beta** -- DONE (00136990). MLPL alpha-beta minimax,
   ~10.8s -> ~0.46s, correct. (P-B.)
2. **memo-dict-primitive** -- add a dict / hashmap value + builtins
   (`dict`, `get`, `set`, `has`) keyed by an array hash, enabling
   transposition tables and dedup (also unblocks `unique`). (P-A.)
3. **interp-alloc** -- hoist loop-invariant constants, reuse small-array
   buffers / arena intermediates, add a scalar fast-path in the op
   dispatch. Bench minimax before/after. (P-D.)
4. **vectorized-dp** (stretch) -- a batched all-states minimax DP as the
   array-idiomatic reference, plus a `where` / `nonzero` primitive
   (boolean mask -> indices) used by `legal`. (P-C, plus the legal-moves
   gap.)

### Saga: tictactoe-mlpl-engine (mostly done)

Replace the `ttt_boards` / `ttt_moves` / `play_vs_random` Rust builtins
with MLPL. DONE so far:

- Engine in MLPL: `u:winner` (incidence matmul), `u:ab` (alpha-beta
  minimax), `u:best_move`, `u:encode`, `u:terminal`
  (`examples/tictactoe-minimax.mlpl`, 0d76c26c).
- Self-play dataset generator + full pipeline (dataset -> train -> play
  -> waffle), all MLPL, verified before/after improvement
  (`examples/tictactoe-demo.mlpl`, 4a1ebb67). `while` accumulation; no
  dedup/memo needed (measured).
- Literate page rewritten to all-MLPL steps (4d177ce6).

DEFERRED (user decision, "org doc all-MLPL now, defer builtin removal"):
removing the `ttt_*` builtins from `mlpl-eval` and re-pointing the
connect-only MLX GPU demo (+ classifier_winrate / play_vs_random tests)
onto the MLPL engine. The MLPL self-play dataset is smaller/slower to
generate than the instant `ttt_boards()` 4520-set, so the GPU demo's
65->0 before/after needs re-tuning on the MLPL dataset before the
builtins can go. Scheduled follow-up.

## Measurement: is the dataset generatable without new primitives? (yes)

"Measure first" before building P-A (dict) or P-C (vectorized). Timed
`best_move` (the per-position label = optimal move) by game depth, with
alpha-beta:

| position        | best_move time |
|-----------------|----------------|
| empty (depth 0) | 0.79s          |
| depth 1         | 0.05s          |
| depth 2         | 0.04-0.06s     |
| depth 3         | 0.01s          |
| depth 5, 7      | < 0.01s        |

The cost collapses after the opening: the empty board is the only
expensive position; everything from move 1 is <= 50ms, from move 3 ~ms.

Implications:

- Labeling all ~4520 unique non-terminal positions ONCE is ~tens of
  seconds (dominated by the single empty board + a handful of depth-1/2
  positions); the deep bulk is ~ms each.
- A workable training dataset can be generated by SELF-PLAY (collect
  positions, label with `best_move`) with NO dedup/memo and NO new
  primitive -- as long as the one expensive position (the empty board)
  is not re-labeled every game (trivially cached or skipped by
  collecting from move >= 1).
- So **P-A (dict) and P-C (vectorized DP) are NOT blockers** for the
  MLPL-native engine; they remain nice-to-haves (exact unique-set
  enumeration, or an elegant batched showcase). Alpha-beta (P-B) was the
  load-bearing fix.

Conclusion: the `tictactoe-mlpl-engine` saga can proceed now with
existing primitives (winner/minimax/best_move done; add `encode` +
self-play dataset + the play loop, then remove the `ttt_*` builtins).

## New findings (during P-B)

- **`break` / `continue` only work in `while`, not `for`.** `break`
  inside a `for` body errors "break used outside of a while loop".
  Workaround: a `done` flag that gates the loop body. Should be lifted
  (loop-control should work in `for` too). Candidate for the
  language-correctness saga's backlog.
- **Deep MLPL recursion uses a lot of interpreter stack.** Tic-tac-toe
  minimax (depth 9) overflows the default debug test-thread stack; the
  release repl and a 64MB test thread are fine. Worth bounding /
  flattening the interpreter's per-call stack usage (part of P-D,
  interpreter work).

## Interim state

Until the above land, the tic-tac-toe demo keeps the Rust builtins
(`ttt_boards`, `ttt_moves`, `play_vs_random`) as a working fast path;
the literate page shows the engine's Rust source as explained listings.
This is a documented stopgap, not the end state -- the end state is the
MLPL engine above.

# LoRA fine-tune on MLX (Saga 15 step 005).
#
# Same source as `demos/lora_finetune.mlpl` with the
# fine-tune training block wrapped in `device("mlx") { ... }`.
# Base pre-training stays on CPU: the Saga 14 MLX ratio at
# Tiny LM scale is slightly slower than CPU per op, and the
# base pre-train is cheap + deterministic on CPU. The
# fine-tune loop is where the MLX story matters -- it is what
# runs in production for a real LoRA workflow.
#
# CLI-only (MLX feature). Run with:
#   cargo run -p mlpl-repl --features mlx --release -- \
#     -f demos/lora_finetune_mlx.mlpl
# Apple Silicon + the `mlx` Cargo feature are required.

# ---- 1. Base model + Shakespeare tokenizer (CPU) ----
corpus = load_preloaded("tiny_shakespeare_snippet")
tok    = train_bpe(corpus, 280, 0)
ids    = apply_tokenizer(tok, corpus)
X_all  = shift_pairs_x(ids, 32)
Y_all  = shift_pairs_y(ids, 32)
X      = reshape(X_all, [reduce_mul(shape(X_all))])
Y      = reshape(Y_all, [reduce_mul(shape(Y_all))])

V = 280 ; d = 32 ; h = 1
base = chain(embed(V, d, 0), residual(chain(rms_norm(d), causal_attention(d, h, 1))), residual(chain(rms_norm(d), linear(d, 128, 2), relu_layer(), linear(128, d, 3))), rms_norm(d), linear(d, V, 4))

experiment "lora_mlx_base_pretrain" {
  train 100 {
    adam(cross_entropy(apply(base, X), Y), base, 0.001, 0.9, 0.999, 0.00000001);
    loss_metric = cross_entropy(apply(base, X), Y)
  }
}

# ---- 2. Synthetic instruction corpus (CPU-side tokenization) ----
instr = "Q: hi A: hello Q: name A: alice Q: bye A: farewell Q: how A: well Q: who A: friend Q: what A: answer Q: where A: here Q: when A: now"
instr_ids = apply_tokenizer(tok, instr)
instr_X_all = shift_pairs_x(instr_ids, 16)
instr_Y_all = shift_pairs_y(instr_ids, 16)
instr_X = reshape(instr_X_all, [reduce_mul(shape(instr_X_all))])

## Where the GPU story stands

The **MLX track is effectively done** (saga `local-gpu-agentic`, steps 004–010): forward + backward + Adam all run on the Apple GPU, and the "MLX LoRA fine-tune" demo is relabeled true-GPU. The architecture it left behind is the template a CUDA track slots into:

| MLX crate | Role | CUDA analog to build |
|---|---|---|
| `mlpl-mlx-rt` | forward ops (`mlx_rs::Array`) | `mlpl-cuda-rt` |
| `mlpl-mlx-forward` | embed / rms_norm / attention / cross-entropy | `mlpl-cuda-forward` |
| `mlpl-mlx-train` | `value_and_grad` + `MlxAdam` (on-device) | `mlpl-cuda-train` |
| `mlpl-mlx-model` | `demo_forward` assembly | `mlpl-cuda-model` |
| `mlpl-mlx-serve` | server-side peer dispatcher | `mlpl-cuda-serve` |

The plumbing is **already CUDA-aware**: `Device::Cuda` exists in the demo registry (rendered visible-but-not-runnable), `Value::DeviceTensor` carries a `device: String` with `"cuda"` called out in comments, and `device("cuda") { … }` already parses and pushes onto the device stack — it just falls back to CPU because no `cuda` dispatch exists. ## The decisive advantage of pivoting now

This box is an **RTX 5060 Ti (Blackwell sm_120, 16 GB), CUDA 13.2 at `/opt/cuda`, 1.6 TB free.** Unlike the MLX track — which this Linux machine can never build or test — **a CUDA track is fully buildable and testable right here, in-session.** TDD with real GPU parity tests, not Apple-only glue I can't run.

## The MLX demos to mirror

3. **`cuda-dispatch-wire`** — generalize `try_mlx_dispatch`/`dispatched_call` so `device("cuda")` routes through `mlpl-cuda-rt`; CPU fallback + one-time warning preserved.
4. **`cuda-forward-primitives` + `cuda-model`** — embed/rms_norm/attention/cross-entropy + `demo_forward`, parity vs CPU.
5. **`cuda-lora-demo`** — first CUDA demo (`lora_finetune_cuda.mlpl`) end-to-end via `eval_adam`'s CUDA branch + its `.org` literate doc; registry entry flips to runnable on a connected CUDA peer.

# Agentic `:ask` -- Saga Plan (tool-using, RLM-like)

## Vision

Today `:ask` sends one context-rich prompt to Ollama. The goal is
to make it **agent-like**: a tool-capable model is given a *meta
context* describing what context is *available on request*, and it
**requests** only what it needs (recent history, a variable's
shape/values, the selected sculpture, a builtin's help, a demo's
source) via tool calls, then answers from what it retrieved. This
is the start of Recursive-Language-Model-style tooling -- the model
drives a retrieval/answer loop instead of being flooded up front.

## Already shipped (the foundation this builds on)

- **Connect-mode evaluator swap (SSE).** `?connect=<url>` routes
  REPL eval to `mlpl-serve`, executed server-side (no browser CORS,
  no WASM `std::time` panic). `connect.rs` + `eval_wasm::connect_eval`.
- **Contextual `:ask`.** Prompt = a "you are inside the sw-MLPL
  REPL" system preamble + recent REPL activity + the selected 3D
  sculpture summary (`window.__stage3d_context()`). Plus `:history`,
  the in-dialog **Ask** button (`window.__mlpl_ask`), and
  configurable `?ollama=` / `?model=`.
- **Ollama tool-calling verified.** Capable models (`llama3.1`,
  `qwen2.5-coder:14b`) return proper `tool_calls`; the tiny
  `qwen2.5:0.5b` emits the call as plain text -- so the agent loop
  needs a strong model (e.g. `qwen2.5-coder:14b` on the LAN box).

## Phase 0 -- Ollama settings exposure (prerequisite)

Make host + model first-class and discoverable rather than
hard-coded / query-string-only:

- **Host:** `localhost:11434` or a LAN host (e.g.
  `http://large12:11434`). The call is server-side, so any host
  reachable from `mlpl-serve` works.
- **Server-owned config:** a `config.toml` (and/or CLI flags /
  `OLLAMA_HOST` env) on `mlpl-serve` holding the default host +
  default model, so the browser carries nothing.
- **List models:** `GET <host>/api/tags` -> a model picker in the
  UI; a `:models ollama` listing (distinct from MLPL `:models`).
- **Default + override:** choose a default model; override per call
  (`:ask --model qwen2.5-coder:14b <question>` and/or a UI
  dropdown). Replaces the current `?ollama=`/`?model=` stopgap.

## Phase 1 -- proper system/user messages

Switch from `/api/generate` with the system text embedded in the
prompt to `/api/chat` with a real `system` message + `user`
message (Ollama supports both). Weak models follow a real system
role far better. Extend `llm_call` (optional `system` arg) or add a
server-side `ask()` builtin.

## Phase 2 -- the tool-using agent loop

Run the loop **server-side** (it owns the live session):

1. `POST <host>/api/chat` with `messages` + `tools` (function defs)
   + the meta-context system prompt ("you have these tools; request
   only what you need; do not guess").
2. If the reply has `tool_calls`, fulfill each from the session and
   append the results as `tool` messages; loop (bounded depth /
   token budget).
3. When the model returns content with no tool calls, that's the
   answer.

**Context-provider tools** (map to existing introspection):

| tool | source |
|------|--------|
| `get_recent_history()` | REPL history (client snapshot) |
| `get_workspace_vars()` | session env (`:vars`) |
| `describe_variable(name)` | `:describe` / inspect |
| `get_selected_sculpture()` | client `__stage3d_context()` snapshot |
| `get_builtin_help(name)` | `:help` table |
| `get_demo_source(name)` | the demo registry |

Client-only context (the 3D selection) is passed as a snapshot in
the initial request so the server can answer those tool calls
without a round-trip to the browser. Surface the tool-call trace in
the UI for transparency ("the model looked at: history, var X").

## Phase 3 -- the RLM demo

A demo that **runs ML steps, then asks for help**:

1. Train a tiny model (or build an attention pattern) -- a few REPL
   lines.
2. Issue an agentic `:ask` ("why did the loss plateau?" / "what does
   this attention pattern show, given my setup?").
3. The model calls `get_recent_history` + `get_workspace_vars` +
   `describe_variable`, then answers from what it retrieved -- the
   visible RLM-like loop.

## Open questions / decisions

- **Model requirement:** tool-capable; default to a strong remote
  one (`qwen2.5-coder:14b` on `large12`). Document the floor.
- **Where the loop lives:** server-side; client passes the 3D
  selection snapshot. (A future variant could let the server call
  back to the client for live UI state.)
- **Flooding control:** per-tool result size caps; the point of the
  meta-context is selective retrieval.
- **Security:** the server makes outbound calls -- allow-list the
  Ollama host(s) in config (mirrors the connect-mode CORS
  allow-list).
- **Live-demo gating:** these features only work in connect mode;
  the GitHub Pages demo should mark them visible-but-not-runnable
  (a `requires_connect` flag on the demo registry -- separate small
  task).

## References

- `docs/using-ollama.md`, `docs/using-cli-server.md` -- LLM + server.
- `components/web-handlers/.../connect.rs` -- current `:ask`.
- `components/runtime-core/.../llm_builtins.rs` -- `call_ollama`.
- Recursive Language Models (external research) -- the inspiration.

# Saga: CUDA foundation (Linux GPU backend)

## Vision

Bring real NVIDIA/CUDA GPU acceleration to sw-MLPL on Linux,
mirroring the now-complete MLX (Apple) track. The end state: a
CUDA-equivalent demo + literate `.org` doc for each MLX demo, and a
UI that connects in `?connect=` mode to an `mlpl-serve` peer running
on a Mac (MLX) AND/OR on an Arch Linux box (CUDA), gating demos by
the device the connected peer actually offers.

This first saga is the **foundation + one demo end-to-end**, proven
on real hardware. A follow-up saga mirrors the remaining MLX demos.

## Why now, why here

This dev host is an **RTX 5060 Ti (Blackwell, sm_120, 16 GB), CUDA
13.2 at `/opt/cuda`, x86_64-linux-gnu, 1.6 TB free**. Unlike the
MLX track -- which this Linux box can never build or test -- a CUDA
track is fully buildable and TDD-testable in-session with real GPU
parity tests, not Apple-only glue.

## Foundation already in place (CUDA-aware plumbing)

- **`Device::Cuda`** exists in the web-demos registry
  (`mlpl-web-demos-types`), rendered visible-but-not-runnable on the
  public live demo.
- **`Value::DeviceTensor { device: String, .. }`** already names
  `"cuda"` as a future device (`mlpl-eval-types`).
- **`device("cuda") { .. }`** already parses and pushes onto
  `Environment::device_stack`; it currently falls back to CPU with a
  one-time warning because no CUDA dispatch exists.
- **Connect mode (SSE)** routes eval to any `mlpl-serve` peer; the
  `peer_dispatcher` abstraction dispatches a whole `device(...)`
  block server-side.

## Backend decision (the analog of MLX step 005's fork)

**Chosen: `candle`** (HuggingFace `candle-core` autograd via
`Tensor::backward()` + `candle-nn` optimizers, on `cudarc`). This
mirrors the MLX track's winning "approach A": use the framework's
built-in autodiff + optimizer, zero hand-written backward formulas.
Pure Rust, no multi-GB libtorch download. The load-bearing risk is
Blackwell sm_120 / CUDA 13.2 support in `cudarc`/`candle` -- the
step-1 spike de-risks exactly that before any wider work.

Rejected: `tch` (libtorch -- heavy + Blackwell/CUDA-13 build
freshness risk) and `cudarc`-only (= MLX "approach B", ~hand-written
kernels + autodiff, explicitly rejected on the MLX track).

## Crate plan (mirror the MLX crates 1:1)

| MLX crate | Role | CUDA crate to build |
|---|---|---|
| `mlpl-mlx-rt` | forward ops | `mlpl-cuda-rt` |
| `mlpl-mlx-forward` | embed / rms_norm / attention / cross-entropy | `mlpl-cuda-forward` |
| `mlpl-mlx-train` | autodiff + on-device Adam | `mlpl-cuda-train` |
| `mlpl-mlx-model` | `demo_forward` assembly | `mlpl-cuda-model` |
| `mlpl-mlx-serve` | server-side peer dispatcher | `mlpl-cuda-serve` |

All CUDA crates triple-gate `cfg(all(feature = "cuda", target_os =
"linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))`; absent any gate, dispatch is a
stub returning `None` and `device("cuda")` falls back to CPU with a
one-time warning (mirror `mlpl-eval/src/device.rs`).

## Steps

1. **cuda-backend-spike** -- add a gated spike crate; prove
   `candle` value/grad (`Tensor::backward`) + an Adam step reduce a
   tiny regression loss ON the RTX 5060 Ti. De-risk sm_120 / CUDA
   13.2 (pin candle/cudarc versions that support it; record the
   build incantation). Parity vs the analytic gradient. This is the
   go/no-go gate for candle.
2. **mlpl-cuda-rt** -- forward ops crate (matmul, elementwise,
   activations, softmax/reduce), gated; parity-tested vs CPU
   (`mlpl-array`).
3. **cuda-dispatch-wire** -- generalize `try_mlx_dispatch` /
   `dispatched_call` in `mlpl-eval/src/device.rs` so `device("cuda")`
   routes through `mlpl-cuda-rt`; CPU fallback + one-time warning
   preserved; device dispatch tests extended for cuda.
4. **cuda-forward-and-model** -- `mlpl-cuda-forward` (embed,
   rms_norm, causal_attention, cross_entropy) + `mlpl-cuda-model`
   (`demo_forward`), each parity-tested vs the CPU primitives and
   the MLX reference.
5. **cuda-lora-demo** -- `mlpl-cuda-train` (candle autodiff +
   on-device Adam) wired into `eval_adam`'s CUDA branch (analog of
   `grad_optim_mlx.rs`); first CUDA demo `demos/lora_finetune_cuda.mlpl`
   + literate `examples/literate/cuda-lora-finetune.org`; flip the
   registry entry to runnable-on-connected-CUDA-peer. Parity: the
   `device("cuda")` LoRA loss curve matches the CPU path within fp32
   tol.
6. **cuda-connect-peer** -- `mlpl-cuda-serve` so
   `mlpl-serve --features cuda` on Linux is a connect-mode peer;
   add a `GET /api/devices` capability probe so the UI knows whether
   a connected server offers `mlx`, `cuda`, or neither, and gates
   demos by the live peer instead of a static guess. This is what
   makes "connect to a Mac and/or this Arch box" honest.

## Out of scope (this saga)

- Mirroring the other 3 MLX demos (tiny_lm, neural_thicket,
  mlx_remote) + their org docs -- a FOLLOW-UP saga once the vertical
  slice is green.
- SmolLM2 loader / LLaMA-style ops (saga `local-gpu-agentic`
  Phases 4-5, now CUDA candidates -- later).
- Agentic `:ask` Phase 2/3 -- parked on `main` as
  `local-gpu-agentic` step 011, platform-agnostic, pick up on
  either host.

## References

- `docs/saga-local-gpu-agentic.md` -- the MLX track this mirrors;
  device tiers, "measurable learning" metric, demo-download policy.
- `mlpl-eval/src/device.rs` -- the single dispatch site to generalize.
- `components/native-rt/crates/mlpl-mlx-{rt,forward,train}`,
  `components/mlx-model/`, `components/serve/.../mlpl-mlx-serve` --
  the crates to mirror.
- candle: <https://github.com/huggingface/candle>;
  cudarc Blackwell/CUDA-13 support is the step-1 spike's job to pin.

# Saga: CUDA foundation (Linux GPU backend)

## Vision

Bring real NVIDIA/CUDA GPU acceleration to sw-MLPL on Linux,
mirroring the now-complete MLX (Apple) track. The end state: a
CUDA-equivalent demo + literate `.org` doc for each MLX demo, and a
UI that connects in `?connect=` mode to an `mlpl-serve` peer running
on a Mac (MLX) AND/OR on an Arch Linux box (CUDA), gating demos by
the device the connected peer actually offers.

This first saga is the **foundation + one demo end-to-end**, proven
on real hardware. A follow-up saga mirrors the remaining MLX demos.

## Why now, why here

This dev host is an **RTX 5060 Ti (Blackwell, sm_120, 16 GB), CUDA
13.2 at `/opt/cuda`, x86_64-linux-gnu, 1.6 TB free**. Unlike the
MLX track -- which this Linux box can never build or test -- a CUDA
track is fully buildable and TDD-testable in-session with real GPU
parity tests, not Apple-only glue.

## Foundation already in place (CUDA-aware plumbing)

- **`Device::Cuda`** exists in the web-demos registry
  (`mlpl-web-demos-types`), rendered visible-but-not-runnable on the
  public live demo.
- **`Value::DeviceTensor { device: String, .. }`** already names
  `"cuda"` as a future device (`mlpl-eval-types`).
- **`device("cuda") { .. }`** already parses and pushes onto
  `Environment::device_stack`; it currently falls back to CPU with a
  one-time warning because no CUDA dispatch exists.
- **Connect mode (SSE)** routes eval to any `mlpl-serve` peer; the
  `peer_dispatcher` abstraction dispatches a whole `device(...)`
  block server-side.

## Backend decision (the analog of MLX step 005's fork)

**Chosen: `candle`** (HuggingFace `candle-core` autograd via
`Tensor::backward()` + `candle-nn` optimizers, on `cudarc`). This
mirrors the MLX track's winning "approach A": use the framework's
built-in autodiff + optimizer, zero hand-written backward formulas.
Pure Rust, no multi-GB libtorch download. The load-bearing risk is
Blackwell sm_120 / CUDA 13.2 support in `cudarc`/`candle` -- the
step-1 spike de-risks exactly that before any wider work.

Rejected: `tch` (libtorch -- heavy + Blackwell/CUDA-13 build
freshness risk) and `cudarc`-only (= MLX "approach B", ~hand-written
kernels + autodiff, explicitly rejected on the MLX track).

## Crate plan (mirror the MLX crates 1:1)

| MLX crate | Role | CUDA crate to build |
|---|---|---|
| `mlpl-mlx-rt` | forward ops | `mlpl-cuda-rt` |
| `mlpl-mlx-forward` | embed / rms_norm / attention / cross-entropy | `mlpl-cuda-forward` |
| `mlpl-mlx-train` | autodiff + on-device Adam | `mlpl-cuda-train` |
| `mlpl-mlx-model` | `demo_forward` assembly | `mlpl-cuda-model` |
| `mlpl-mlx-serve` | server-side peer dispatcher | `mlpl-cuda-serve` |

All CUDA crates triple-gate `cfg(all(feature = "cuda", target_os =
"linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))`; absent any gate, dispatch is a
stub returning `None` and `device("cuda")` falls back to CPU with a
one-time warning (mirror `mlpl-eval/src/device.rs`).

## Steps

1. **cuda-backend-spike** -- add a gated spike crate; prove
   `candle` value/grad (`Tensor::backward`) + an Adam step reduce a
   tiny regression loss ON the RTX 5060 Ti. De-risk sm_120 / CUDA
   13.2 (pin candle/cudarc versions that support it; record the
   build incantation). Parity vs the analytic gradient. This is the
   go/no-go gate for candle.
2. **mlpl-cuda-rt** -- forward ops crate (matmul, elementwise,
   activations, softmax/reduce), gated; parity-tested vs CPU
   (`mlpl-array`).
3. **cuda-dispatch-wire** -- generalize `try_mlx_dispatch` /
   `dispatched_call` in `mlpl-eval/src/device.rs` so `device("cuda")`
   routes through `mlpl-cuda-rt`; CPU fallback + one-time warning
   preserved; device dispatch tests extended for cuda.
4. **cuda-forward-and-model** -- `mlpl-cuda-forward` (embed,
   rms_norm, causal_attention, cross_entropy) + `mlpl-cuda-model`
   (`demo_forward`), each parity-tested vs the CPU primitives and
   the MLX reference.
5. **cuda-lora-demo** -- `mlpl-cuda-train` (candle autodiff +
   on-device Adam) wired into `eval_adam`'s CUDA branch (analog of
   `grad_optim_mlx.rs`); first CUDA demo `demos/lora_finetune_cuda.mlpl`
   + literate `examples/literate/cuda-lora-finetune.org`; flip the
   registry entry to runnable-on-connected-CUDA-peer. Parity: the
   `device("cuda")` LoRA loss curve matches the CPU path within fp32
   tol.
6. **cuda-connect-peer** -- `mlpl-cuda-serve` so
   `mlpl-serve --features cuda` on Linux is a connect-mode peer;
   add a `GET /api/devices` capability probe so the UI knows whether
   a connected server offers `mlx`, `cuda`, or neither, and gates
   demos by the live peer instead of a static guess. This is what
   makes "connect to a Mac and/or this Arch box" honest.

## Out of scope (this saga)

- Mirroring the other 3 MLX demos (tiny_lm, neural_thicket,
  mlx_remote) + their org docs -- a FOLLOW-UP saga once the vertical
  slice is green.
- SmolLM2 loader / LLaMA-style ops (saga `local-gpu-agentic`
  Phases 4-5, now CUDA candidates -- later).
- Agentic `:ask` Phase 2/3 -- parked on `main` as
  `local-gpu-agentic` step 011, platform-agnostic, pick up on
  either host.

## References

- `docs/saga-local-gpu-agentic.md` -- the MLX track this mirrors;
  device tiers, "measurable learning" metric, demo-download policy.
- `mlpl-eval/src/device.rs` -- the single dispatch site to generalize.
- `components/native-rt/crates/mlpl-mlx-{rt,forward,train}`,
  `components/mlx-model/`, `components/serve/.../mlpl-mlx-serve` --
  the crates to mirror.
- candle: <https://github.com/huggingface/candle>;
  cudarc Blackwell/CUDA-13 support is the step-1 spike's job to pin.
